mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 90 P300 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Land Rover Defender 90 P300 typically ranges from £4,200 to £6,500 for supply only, depending on the specialist and the extent of upgrades included. Used engines start around £1,500 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing AJ200P/204PT engine in a Land Rover Defender 90 P300?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Land Rover Defender 90 P300 are unexplained coolant loss, a distinct rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold starts (timing chain rattle), or illuminated temperature warning lights. You should also check for sweet-smelling exhaust or oil residue around the valve cover.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Defender 90 P300?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the strong modern 4x4 market, a well-maintained Land Rover Defender 90 P300 typically holds a value between £45,000 and £70,000+, making a £4,200 to £6,500 rebuilt engine a financially sound investment. A rebuilt engine restores reliability, preserves resale value, and is significantly cheaper than purchasing a newer vehicle.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 90 P300 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Land Rover Defender 90 P300 typically takes 2 to 4 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the cooling system are being upgraded simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt unit may add a few days, so always confirm the exact turnaround time with your chosen specialist.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Land Rover Defender 90 P300 and the D250 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Land Rover Defender 90 P300 uses a 2.0-litre turbocharged inline-4 petrol engine (AJ200P/204PT) producing 300 PS, prioritising smooth, responsive performance and refinement. In contrast, the D250 uses a 2.0-litre turbocharged diesel engine (204DTD) focused on low-end torque and fuel economy for heavy towing or off-road use.
